We need to find minimum sum of absolute deviations from a palindromic integer y (positive) less than 10^9.

Given array of length up to 1e5, each nums[i] up to 1e9.

Goal: choose a palindrome y (positive integer < 10^9) minimizing sum_i |nums[i] - y|.

This is essentially 1D L1 minimization: the optimal y is median of nums (any value between lower median and upper median) when minimizing sum of absolute differences.

But we have restriction that y must be palindrome.

Therefore we need to find palindrome y minimizing sum_i |nums[i] - y|. This is like find median then find nearest palindrome(s) to median, but need to consider that sum of absolute differences function is convex piecewise linear with slope changes at each nums[i]. So minimal sum occurs at any median; if median not palindrome, need to find palindrome nearest to median in terms of minimizing sum (i.e., the value y that is palindrome that gives minimal sum). Since sum|a_i - y| is convex and minimized over real line at median. For integer y, the optimum is any integer median (if n odd median is middle; if even any integer between two middle values yields same minimal sum). So we can find candidate palindromes near median: the nearest palindrome <= median, and nearest palindrome >= median. Actually we might need to consider more if there are gaps due to palindrome distribution? Since convex function, the minimal over a discrete set (palindromes) will be attained at palindrome closest to the median (in terms of value). Indeed for convex function f(y) = sum |a_i - y|, which is convex and piecewise linear with slope monotonic increasing: derivative (subgradient) is -#(a_i > y) + #(a_i < y). The minimum region is where derivative crosses zero: any y such that #less <= n/2 and #greater <= n/2 (i.e., median interval). For convex function, minimizing over a discrete set S yields the point in S nearest to the minimizer interval (any point in that interval gives same minimal value).
